title: Mixed review: a seeded, sendable mix of skills from any grades and areas (new page type, PAGE_TYPES 5.5 proposed)

engine.plan: js/modules/sheet/roles/mixed-practice.js (GROUPED shelves, the M1 mixed arrangement, interleave.js dealCounts / interleave)
engine.rules: js/modules/sheet/roles/review.js (PT-REV-2 supports at level 1, no steps / models / traces; letters off: numbered 1..N)
engine.host: js/modules/print-sheet.js buildSheet (ROLE_ALIASES entry mixed-review -> mixed-practice with input.review)

teaches: Retrieval of skills already taught: a short sheet of 5 to 30 problems drawn from the grades and maths areas the teacher ticks, each problem in its own skill's cell at review supports (PT-REV-2), numbered 1..N, scored, with a facsimile answer key and a key summary by area and skill. On screen the same N problems play as a practice card, an online worksheet, a scored quiz and the boss / race games.
summary: A new page type that is a CONFIGURATION of the mixed-practice engine, not a second engine: a pure pool / deal module turns the teacher's filters (grades, areas, only 8/10 skills, unticked skills, from my lessons) and a seed into an explicit list of N items {categoryId, skillId, opts, seed}; buildSheet lays that list out with mixed-practice.js in review mode; every screen host plays the same list. A share code carries the list, the counts, the order and the seed, so the mix is reproduced exactly.
research: No premium logins this round (the card writer has no browser). From knowledge of the reference sites: MathWorksheets4Kids 'mixed review' / 'spiral review' grade packs (a fixed mix of 10-20 items across strands per page, an answer key), K5 Learning 'mixed operations' and grade-level 'review' worksheets, IXL's 'recommendations' and 'skill plans' (screen-side choice of weak skills, per-skill score report), Math-Drills mixed-operation sheets (seeded 'new set' button). Converted to our design: 6-12 problems a page, not 30-50 (12.1); one boxed cell per problem in its own skill's cell; numbers, not letters (PT-MIX-7); the pupil page never names the area (ruling 13). The research must be repeated with the logins before the build (CLAUDE.md MANDATORY step) by lane MR-B.
problemTypes: No new problem type: each item is its own skill's cell at level 1 (PT-REV-2) with its own instruction in the cell or its band strip (PT-MIX-4, PT-MIX-5).
The mix itself: N items over k skills, k = min(|pool|, ceil(N / 3)), 2 or 3 items each (dealCounts min 2), no skill over half the sheet unless the pool has one skill (refused).
progression: Order mixed (default): interleaved, no two items of one skill side by side where the pool allows (interleave maxRun 1).
Order easy -> hard: by placement grade K..6+, then data.js teaching order.
Order by area: AREA_ORDER (CC, OA, NBT, NF, MEAS, DATA, G, RPNS, WORDS), easy -> hard inside an area.

drawing.sizes: M and L only (owner 2026-11-13; S dropped: a stored S or an S code reads as M). Look Daily (mixed-practice DEFAULT_LOOK). Lattice N: Daily 6 at M, 4 at L (AUTO_N); I Can 8 / 6 when a lesson asks for it. Shelves at most 7 at M, 5 at L (12.1). Problems per page at most 12 at M, 10 at L (12.1 Review 12 / 8-12; DN-1 20 at L).

capacity.Lwide: 1 sheet 2-up when the 5 fit a half page, else 1 page (5)

notes: Typical mix = shelves of 2 to 3 cells (stacks, equations, small visuals): per page M 12, L 8. All-compact (facts, one-line equations): M 12, L 10. All-wide (number lines, coin rows, word problems, one cell a shelf): M 7, L 5.
pages = ceil(N / per-page), the items split as evenly as whole shelves allow (largest page first, paginate.js rebalanced last page), never a page under half of another (H5).
The engine measures; the dialog never plans pages (L16). These rows are the planning targets the checks hold the measured pages to.
Key pages = pupil pages (facsimile, PT-KEY-1) + the key summary: under the last key page's grid when its rows fit (rows x 7 mm + 14), else one more key page. A week adds one weekly table page.

N = 5 prints 2-up (lead ruling 2026-11-19, R7): the same 5 items twice on one sheet, each half with its own header (Name, Date, Score ___/5), a dashed cut line between; the key is 2-up the same way. When the 5 items do not fit a half page (all-wide at L), one full page of 5 with the shelves grown to the fill limit.

ownerRulings.ruling: A new paper type plus a playable mode, MIXED REVIEW: any mix of grades (school placement, chips derived, K-6+); any mix of the 9 areas with CCSS domain labels; optional untick of single skills; 'Only 8/10 skills' ON by default, read from redesign-passed.js; 5 / 10 / 15 / 20 / 25 / 30 problems; a seeded random mix with a 'New mix' button; every sheet has an answer key.
ownerRulings.source: owner 2026-11-14, relayed by the lead (lf-mixreview brief)

ownerRulings.ruling: Built on the EXISTING mixed-practice engine (sheet/roles/mixed-practice.js) and the review role (sheet/roles/review.js). No second engine.
SENDABLE: a share code / link reproduces the identical mix; it extends the existing share-code systems append-only.
PLAYABLE: practice card, online worksheet, quiz (scored) and the game modes.

All five improvements: (1) a Mon-Fri weekly set; (2) spaced / weak-skill weighting on screen; (3) the key and the results tagged by skill with a per-domain breakdown; (4) order mixed / easy -> hard / by area; (5) a 'From my lessons' pool.
Screens are print, computer / Chromebook 1280-1366 px and tablet 820-1024 px; no 390 px. Print sizes M and L only; S dropped (an S setting or code falls back to M).

misconceptions.error: Carries the last item's procedure into the next one (adds on a subtract item after an add item): the interleaving is the point; the cell's own sign and instruction must be visible in every cell (PT-MIX-5 cue), never only in a band strip of another skill
Reads item difficulty from position (easy -> hard order) and stops at the first hard one: the default order is mixed; easy -> hard is the teacher's choice
The teacher reads one total as mastery: the key summary and results split the score by area and skill so a 7/10 that is 4/4 place value and 0/3 time is seen as such

options: grades: chips K, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6+ (multi, 'All'); a skill's chips = its school placement (the school grades whose pacing lessons link it) plus its data.js grade; 6+ = grade 6; default = the Skills screen's grade selection (mq_teacher_skills_ui), else Grade 2; each chip shows its pool count; a 0 chip is shown, greyed, with its count.

areas: 9 chips CC, OA, NBT, NF, MEAS, DATA, G, RPNS, WORDS, each labelled from AREA_LABELS (card areaLabels, exact): Counting & Cardinality / Operations & Algebraic Thinking / Number & Operations in Base Ten / Number & Operations—Fractions (decimals live here) / Measurement (Measurement & Data) / Data (Measurement & Data) / Geometry / Ratios & Proportional Relationships / The Number System (grade 6) / Words (maths vocabulary); default all on. MIXED and NOSTD skills are never in the pool (lead ruling 2026-11-19, R1).

onlyPassed: on / off; default OFF while the passed pool is small (lead ruling 2026-11-19, R6); the toggle stays visible with its live count, 'Only 8/10 ✓ (32)' = |pool before this filter ∩ REDESIGN_PASSED|; every passed skill in the picker shows a ✓ beside its name whatever the toggle; on = the id is in REDESIGN_PASSED (redesign-passed.js), read live.
skills: the pool list with a tick per skill; default all ticked; stored as an exclusion list (unticked ids), so a skill that joins the pool later is ticked.

fromLessons: off / 'unit' (this school unit to date) / '4w' (the last 4 school weeks) / 'year' (school year to date); default off; source = the school pacing (wrm-links LESSONS + weekForDate), never pupil data (P-RV-9).
order: mixed / easyhard / area; default mixed.
week: off / monfri; default off; week number 1-40, default the school week of the first ticked grade (weekForDate).
New mix: a button, not an option: a new seed (freshSeed 100000-999999); the seed is shown in the teacher footer and carried by the code.
size: M / L; default the teacher's print default (printDefaults().size; L when unset, PT-DLG-5).
key: print on / off; default on; the key is always built, shown in the preview and reachable from the code (PT-KEY-1).

adapt (screen only): off / on; default ON when a pupil starts Mixed review on their own device, OFF on a teacher's link unless the teacher ticks 'Adapt to each pupil' (P1 token); never on print. This is the NAMED exception EX-MXR-ADAPT to PT-DLG-26 / P-RV-9 (owner request 2026-11-14; lead ruling 2026-11-19, R2).

Not offered on this page type: look (Daily fixed), columns (Auto: the lattice decides), anchors / worked examples (PT-REV-2), arrangement (the order option replaces it), per-skill option editing in v1 (each skill at its defaults or its preset's values; ruling 8), Photocopy-safe and paper follow the job as on every role.

share.form: Direct Play link / enhanced skill code: ?c=<skills>|<tokens>
share.skills: the DEALT list in deal order, each the frozen 2-char code + its item count as the existing weight digits + its ~option suffix (EA3~C78). The counts are explicit, so the deal is never re-run on decode.
newTokens: V1  mixed review, format 1 (absent: an ordinary enhanced code)
O<e|a>  order easy -> hard / by area (absent: mixed)
Y<week>  a Mon-Fri week set, the week number (absent: one sheet); the skills part is then the week's union with week totals
K<1-5>  one day of a week code (absent with Y: the whole week)
P1  adapt to each pupil on screen (absent: off; the identical mix)
share.reused: N<n> problem count (5-30), G<p|b|r|w> host (practice card / boss / race / online worksheet), H, T as today.
share.compat: Append-only: no frozen code, position or token meaning changes; a code with none of the new tokens decodes byte-for-byte as before (ws-code-snapshot, ws-share-options). An OLD app skips V / S / O / Y / K / P (parseEnhancedSkillCode's switch ignores unknown keys) and plays the same skills with the same weights as an ordinary mixed set: the skills survive, the identical items do not (stated, not hidden). The quiz host uses the existing ?quiz= share of a quiz built from the mix.
share.identical: Same code + same release => byte-identical items on every host: item i is generateQuestionFor({category, skill, opts, seed: deriveSeed('mixed-review', S, day, i)}). A later release that changes a generator may change numbers; the skills, counts, order and seed never change (MIX-REVIEW-SHARE pins both).

week: Five sheets Mon-Fri of N problems each. Day d seed = deriveSeed('mixed-review-week', S, d). The pool is shuffled by S into a cycle; each day takes the next k skills (wrapping), so every pool skill appears before any skill repeats; no skill on two consecutive days unless |pool| < 2k; from Wednesday one skill a day is the comeback of a skill from two days before (spacing) when the pool allows. Print: 5 pupil sheets (tab 'Week n | Mon' ... 'Fri', footer code with K1-K5), then 5 keys, then one weekly key table (PT-KEY-5: areas and skills as rows, days as columns, item numbers in the cells). Each day reprints exactly from its day code (P-RV-13). One link opens the week with a day picker; a day link opens that day.
weighting: EX-MXR-ADAPT, the named screen-only exception to PT-DLG-26 / P-RV-9 (owner request 2026-11-14; lead ruling 2026-11-19, R2): never printed, never sent, never a teacher record, OFF on teacher links unless 'Adapt to each pupil' (P1). Screen only, adapt on. w(skill) = 1 + due + weak, due = 1 when spacedRepetition[skillId].nextReview <= today (+1 more at box 1 or 2), weak = 1 when skillProgress[skillId].total >= 5 and mastery < 70; a skill with no record is 1; w in 1..4. w is the probability weight of the seeded sample of k skills from the pool AND the dealCounts weight of the N items. Read once at start (a snapshot), so the session's list is fixed; results go back through the normal updateSkillProgress / updateSpacedRepetition path every host already calls. Never on print, never in a teacher record (PT-DLG-26), keyed by bare skillId as progress.js keys it today (ruling 2).
breakdown: KEY: the facsimile pages (answers in the slots, item numbers as on the pupil page), then the key summary table (Andika, black and white, teacher type 11 / 12 pt at M / L): columns Area (name + CCSS domain code) | Skill (label) | Items (numbers) | Score ___ / n; one subtotal row per area ___ / n_area; a total row ___ / N. Under the last key page's grid when its rows fit, else its own key page. RESULTS (worksheet score card, quiz results, game end screen): 'By area' rows (area name + icon; screen chrome may use the area colour, PT-SCR-1) with correct / total and the item numbers, each expandable to its skills, weakest first; the quiz results extend the existing skillAnalysis with the area grouping. Per-skill and per-area subtotals always sum to N.
orderModes: mixed: screen order = interleave(items, weights, S, {maxRun: 1}); print = the M1 mixed arrangement when the dealt skills share one size class (mixedClass ok), else GROUPED shelves whose ORDER is seeded so that no two shelves of one skill are adjacent (a shelf-level interleave; the M2 block packer is not needed). easyhard: shelves and items by placement grade, then data.js position. area: AREA_ORDER, then easy -> hard. Numbering 1..N row-major on paper; the screen hosts play items in the printed number order, so item 7 is the same problem everywhere.
lessonsPool: fromLessons on: for each ticked grade g, the lessons of g's school sequence (wrm-links LESSONS with seq and weeks) whose week is inside the window ending at weekForDate(g, today) -> their WRM steps -> the skills linked 'direct' for those steps in data/curriculum/links/<YEAR>.json, plus skillsForWrmStep(step) from SKILL_WRM. Then the area, only-8/10 and untick filters apply as usual. Outside the school year (no week): 'year' = the whole sequence, 'unit' / '4w' say 'No school week today' and fall back to 'year'. No pupil data, no teacher records.

checks.measures: Sweep (L21, L22): every N in {5,10,15,20,25,30} x size M, L x order x 3 seeds x 12 seeded pools (one-class, mixed classes, all-wide, all-facts, 2-skill pool). On the MEASURED rendered pupil pages: exactly N numbered scored cells 1..N, the Score denominator N, pages within the capacity table, no page over 12 / 10 problems or 7 / 5 shelves, no page under half of another (H5); N = 5 is one 2-up sheet (two identical halves, a cut line, each half /5) unless the items do not fit a half page, no split cell; the key has the same N cells in the same places (PT-KEY-1) plus the summary.
checks.fail: the item count differs from N on any print (e.g. the page filled to shelves x k = 14 for N = 10), a page over the ceiling, a lone-shelf continuation page, a key whose cell count differs.; an N = 5 sheet printed as one half-empty page when its items fit 2-up
checks.backtest: commit-pair: FAIL on master d3830882 (mixed-practice fills the page and ignores the count: a mixed-review request of 10 returns shelves x k), PASS on the lane's build commit.

checks.measures: Node, no browser: for 200 seeded filter sets, every dealt skill is live (not retired, not a tombstone), matches a ticked grade by placement and a ticked area, is in REDESIGN_PASSED when only-8/10 is on (default OFF: a request without the flag deals non-passed skills too), is not unticked, is in the lessons window when fromLessons is on; k = min(|pool|, ceil(N/3)) distinct skills, each 2-3 items, none over half; the order mode holds (mixed: no adjacent pair of one skill where avoidable; easyhard: grades non-decreasing; area: AREA_ORDER non-decreasing); adapt weights from a progress fixture give each weak / due skill at least its share; print requests never read progress. Picker: every REDESIGN_PASSED skill in the list carries the ✓ mark and no other does; the toggle's count equals |filtered pool ∩ REDESIGN_PASSED|.
checks.fail: a non-8/10 skill dealt with the toggle on, an unticked or retired skill dealt, a grade or area outside the filters, an order mode violated, a print request whose deal changes when the progress fixture changes.; a default request that drops non-passed skills (the old ON default); a passed skill without its ✓ or a ✓ on a non-passed skill; a toggle count that differs from the pool
checks.backtest: fixture: the FAIL fixture is a deal that includes a skill outside REDESIGN_PASSED with onlyPassed on and reads skillProgress on a print request; the PASS fixture is the correct deal.

checks.measures: Encode -> decode -> rebuild for 100 seeded mixes (single sheets and weeks, every order, adapt off): the same skill list, counts, order, seed and the same item text and answers (sha of the items) on decode; every pre-existing code in tests/baselines decodes byte-identically (ws-code-snapshot, ws-share-options); master's parseEnhancedSkillCode reads a new code without error and returns the same skills (the old-app degrade).
checks.fail: a code that omits the seed or carries the filters instead of the list (the rebuild differs), a moved or changed old code, an old decoder that throws.
checks.backtest: fixture: FAIL on a fixture codec that writes the filters and no S token (the rebuild deals another mix); PASS on the lane's codec.

checks.measures: Browser, one row a host: one code opened in print (pupil + key), practice card at 1366 and 820, online worksheet at 1366 and 820, quiz (built from the mix and taken), boss and race: the same N items in the same order with the same answers as the print key; every answer box is a slot of the cell (ws-screen-slots), 48 px touch targets at 820; the quiz scores out of N; no console errors; no 390 px row.
checks.fail: a host that generates unseeded (generateQuestion) so its items differ from the key, a host with fewer or more than N items, a quiz scored out of another total.
checks.backtest: commit-pair (browser): FAIL on master d3830882 (a mixed-review code opens as plain mixed play with unseeded items), PASS on the build commit.

checks.measures: Node + one print sweep: a week gives 5 sheets with tabs Mon-Fri and distinct day seeds; no two days identical; every pool skill appears once before any repeats; no skill on two consecutive days unless |pool| < 2k; each day rebuilt alone from its K<d> code equals that day of the week build byte for byte (L24: the week reuses the plan, never re-runs it differently); the weekly key table has every dealt item exactly once.
checks.fail: days that share one seed or repeat a sheet, a pool skill missing from the week while another repeats, a day code that rebuilds a different sheet from the week's.
checks.backtest: fixture: FAIL on a week fixture built with one seed for all five days; PASS on the lane's week builder.

checks.measures: Every key and every results screen of the HOSTS sweep: each item is tagged with its skill and its area (areaOf), the per-skill and per-area subtotals each sum to N (and to the score on screen), the area rows are the areas of the dealt skills in AREA_ORDER, the key summary's item numbers equal skillItemMap(plan), the screen breakdown's numbers equal the key's.
checks.fail: an item missing from the summary or listed twice, an item under the wrong area, subtotals that do not sum to N, a results screen whose per-area numbers differ from the key's.
checks.backtest: fixture: FAIL on a summary fixture where one item is mapped to the wrong area and the area subtotal is short by one; PASS on the lane's summary.

rulings.ruling: From my lessons: default window '4w' when turned on; source = the school pacing (P-RV-9).

rulings.q: Does the owner rule 'a distinct option is also a findable skill' apply?
rulings.ruling: No preset skill and no new tags: mixed review is a page type, findable as 'mixed review', 'spiral review', 'review sheet' in the print picker.

rulings.q: Should the pupil page name the area (band titles 'Place value', 'Time')?
rulings.ruling: The pupil page never names the area: instruction strips only; the key summary, footer CCSS codes and results name them.

rulings.q: May the teacher turn the key off?
rulings.ruling: The key print may be unticked (default on); it is always built, previewed and reachable from the code (PT-KEY-1).

rulings.q: Defaults: 10 problems, order mixed, size = the teacher's print default (L when unset), week off, fromLessons off?
rulings.ruling: Defaults: 10 problems, order mixed, size = the teacher's print default (L when unset), week off, from my lessons off, only 8/10 off.

rulings.q: Signing: ws-spec-card has no page-type kind, so this card has no machine block and --check-signed cannot verify it.
rulings.ruling: The card stays hand-written (kind page-type) and is signed by hand; lane MR-E may later add a page-type kind to ws-spec-card and regenerate it.
